newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister sees delay in VAT cuts to 1998.
newsitem.headline: French minister sees delay in VAT cuts to 1998.

text.p: Any cuts in France's value added tax (VAT) would be delayed to 1998, due to the state of public finances, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday.

"Without doubt public finances will make it more difficult to cut VAT, or less quickly than we would have wanted to. Perhaps there may be in the 1998 budget some lowering of VAT," he told a Forum de l'Expansion business conference.

"Without doubt we could have gone faster today if public finances were in better shape," he said. "It really is towards lower VAT that we have to go and the government will aim for that year after year," he added.
The Socialist party promised VAT cuts during its election campaign as a way of boosting spending power, especially among poorer households.
